### Relationships
The modification addresses a resource management issue by ensuring that the reference taken by `of_find_device_by_node()` is properly released when it is no longer needed. This change is crucial for preventing memory leaks and ensuring that device references are managed correctly in the error handling paths of the `qmp_get` function.         You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by the lack of a `put_device()` call in the error handling path of the `qmp_get` function, which meant that the reference taken by `of_find_device_by_node()` was not released when the device data could not be retrieved. This oversight could lead to memory leaks and improper resource management.
        
        Commit message:
        soc: qcom: aoss: Fix missing put_device call in qmp_get

The reference taken by 'of_find_device_by_node()' must be released when
not needed anymore.
Add the corresponding 'put_device()' in the error handling paths.

Fixes: 8c75d585b931 ("soc: qcom: aoss: Expose send for generic usecase")
Signed-off-by: Miaoqian Lin <linmq006@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Bjorn Andersson <bjorn.andersson@linaro.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220108095931.21527-1-linmq006@gmail.com  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_aoss.c b/drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_aoss.c
index cbe5e39fdaeb..563ae0a501dc 100644
--- a/drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_aoss.c
+++ b/drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_aoss.c
@@ -451,7 +451,11 @@ struct qmp *qmp_get(struct device *dev)
 
 	qmp = platform_get_drvdata(pdev);
 
-	return qmp ? qmp : ERR_PTR(-EPROBE_DEFER);
+	if (!qmp) {
+		put_device(&pdev->dev);
+		return ERR_PTR(-EPROBE_DEFER);
+	}
+	return qmp;
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL(qmp_get);
 
--
